result.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents
result.summary: Memory enables language agents to carry useful distinctions from past experience into future decisions. Its value depends on which distinctions survive, whether a bounded agent can use them, and what can be recovered or revised as demands evolve. We develop a decision-theoretic framework that follows this value from raw history through persistent state, operational use, and costly recovery and revision. Original and retained value are expressed in units of avoided task loss; risk-cost frontiers describe attainable recovery and preservation across uses. Unknown demand yields value profiles, while interactive feedback changes the distribution of future work. A cost-aware simulation condition and five minimal counterexamples expose the roles of information timing, retrieval access, component interaction, feedback and demand uncertainty. In particular, a pointer with zero mutual information about the answer can still reduce the cost of exact recovery. Diagnostics on LoCoMo, a two-project update task and longitudinal cases exhibit failures of preservation, use and measurement. At fixed retrieved evidence, a saved ledger changes subsequent answers; at fixed agent outputs, an evaluator revision changes scores. The framework connects these distinctions to operational risk bounds and testable principles for allocating memory, preserving recovery options and revising evidence dependencies.

AI.brief_summary: 文章提出一个决策论框架，以“避免的任务损失”为单位度量记忆从原始历史到持久状态、实际操作使用以及有成本的恢复与修订中的价值，借助风险—成本前沿、价值剖面、模拟条件和若干反例分析信息时序、检索可得性、反馈与需求不确定性，并在 LoCoMo 和更新任务上诊断记忆保留、使用与测量层面的失败。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“哪些区分得以留存、受限主体能否使用、能否恢复”的问题表述可对应 LVR 内部状态保留哪些视觉区分与信息坍缩，风险—成本前沿及“评估者修订即改变分数”的诊断可供核查 latent 内容实际贡献与评价测量方式，但迁移到多模态推理尚需较多转换。
